title: The Great Wall of China
text: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the historical northern borders of China to protect against raids from various nomadic groups. The wall was built, rebuilt, and maintained from the 7th century BCE to the 17th century CE. The most well-known sections were built by the Ming dynasty (1368–1644). The total length of all the sections is approximately 21,196 km, though the most famous continuous section is about 6,259 km. The wall runs through the northern part of China, traversing mountains, plateaus, and plains. It is one of the most iconic structures in human history and was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
